sentences.text: The name Tochisaurus translates to "ostrich lizard" because its foot functioned with only two weight-bearing toes.
The holotype specimen, which serves as the primary reference for the species, originates from the Maastrichtian-aged Nemegt Formation.
Measuring 242 millimetres in metatarsus length, this animal is regarded as a relatively large member of the troodontid group.
Estimates based on partial metatarsals suggest the creature reached approximately 3 meters in length, stood 0.8 meters high, and weighed nearly 50 kilograms.
The second metatarsal bone is notably reduced and narrow, with a recorded length of 222 millimetres.
The upper surface of the metatarsus slopes forward and downward.
The holotype consists solely of a left metatarsus, marking the first discovery of this bone type for an Asian troodontid.
Notably, the first metatarsal bone is absent from the preserved holotype fossil.
Remains of this dinosaur were uncovered in 1948 by a Soviet-Mongolian expedition working in the Gobi Desert near Nemegt.
The species was formally named Tochisaurus nemegtensis by Kurzanov and Osmólska in 1991.
The specific holotype was located in the Nemegt Formation near Omnogov, Mongolia, during that same 1948 expedition.
The top of the fossil exhibits damage that was once repaired using an unskilled restoration technique.
The inclined proximal surface of the metatarsals and the strong reduction of the second metatarsal suggest the metatarsal claw was not particularly large.
Tochisaurus is classified within the family Troodontidae.
This animal lived during the Maastrichtian stage, a period spanning between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
